narrative.overview:
The page is the printed hoarding around a live building site. The product is what you watch through the round viewing window cut into it. Clay panels fill the page edge to edge, with a joint every 300px. Ivory sign boards are fixed to the panels, and the type is billboard-scale ink set in a condensed grotesque. The hoarding is loud and graphic. The window is the only place where the work shows: an isometric frame whose elements light up in clay while the answer is pinned to them.

The hierarchy is deliberately one-sided. The question is set huge, the answer much smaller, and a dense ruled site information board closes the page. Everything is printed: the clay, the seams and the signs stay the same in light and dark mode. Only the boards and the view through the window dim. The signage carries real content. Blue mandatory signs are what you can ask, clay ring-and-slash signs are what the data cannot answer, and the closing is a two-leaf ink gate set into the hoarding.

The owner has rejected two things for this surface: drawing-sheet frames and grids, and a black navigation bar across the top.
keyCharacteristics: Clay field edge to edge, with a panel joint every 300px (a 2px dark gap and a 1px lit edge).
Condensed Barlow Semi Condensed headlines in ink at billboard scale; Barlow for reading.
Ivory boards fixed to the panels with soft drop shadows; the window and the gate are cut in with inset depth.
Site-signage grammar: blue discs for "can", clay ring-and-slash for "can't".
One clock (150ms beat) drives the whole demo.

rules.name: The Pinned Palette Rule
rules.body: Claude's palette is the owner's commitment: clay, ink, ivory, sky and cloudy, plus their deepened or lightened steps. Do not add new hues.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Clay Rule
rules.body: Text printed on clay is always #0a0a09 (4.7:1 at body size). Do not set #141413, graphite or ivory text on clay.

rules.name: The Printed Hoarding Rule
rules.body: Clay, its joints and the coloured sign bands do not change in dark mode. Only the boards, the window's site, its lines and the pin change.

rules.name: The One Shout Rule
rules.body: The hero question is the only display-scale line in the first viewport. The answer is set at a fraction of that size.

rules.name: The 300px Panel Rule
rules.body: Hoarding joints repeat at exactly 300px, wide enough to read as panels rather than stripes. Do not tighten them.

rules.name: The Fixed-or-Cut Rule
rules.body: Every surface either stands on the hoarding (drop shadow) or is cut into it (inset). Nothing floats.

rules.name: The One Clock Rule
rules.body: Every duration is a multiple of `--beat` (150ms), and the script reads the same variable. Typing runs at a third of a beat, tags land one per beat, the iris takes 3 beats and an answer holds for 26. With reduced motion, the first scene is shown static.

rules.name: The Exact Match Rule
rules.body: The demo uses only real answers from the sample models, and the number of lit elements equals the number stated (17 level-2 beams, 9 walls, 17 concrete pieces).

rules.name: The Understood-not-Executed Rule
rules.body: The demo shows how a question was understood, as tags. It never shows the query or the SQL.

dos: Do set every piece of text on clay in print ink (#0a0a09).
Do keep the hoarding, its 300px joints and the sign bands the same in both colour schemes; dim only the boards and the window.
Do make every surface either fixed onto the hoarding (drop shadow) or cut into it (inset with a clay-deep edge).
Do use blue discs for what Augmented can do and clay ring-and-slash signs for what it cannot, each with real content.
Do time every animation in multiples of `--beat` (150ms) and provide a static reduced-motion state.
Do use only real sample-model answers, with lit elements matching the stated count.
donts: Don't add drawing-sheet frames, title blocks or background grid lines to the landing page (the owner rejected them; that system belongs to the app pages).
Don't put an ink bar across the top of the page; the masthead sits on the clay.
Don't show the internal query or SQL anywhere public; show understood tags instead.
Don't introduce colours outside Claude's palette.
Don't add decorative hardware (bolts, screws, backing mats) to boards; they were removed in the finish review.
Don't set clay as text at body size on ivory; use it only for large bold numerals.
